rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir calls the preceding report exceptionally strange and unique to al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman.
rows.anchor: هذا حديث غريب جدا، وسياق عجيب، تفرد به القاسم بن عبد الرحمن هذا

rows.speaker: يحيى بن معين
rows.claim: Yahya ibn Ma'in judged al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman worthless as a transmitter.
rows.anchor: وقد قال فيه يحيى بن معين: "ليس يساوي شيئا"

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم الرازي
rows.claim: Abu Hatim al-Razi weakened al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman.
rows.anchor: وضعفه أبو حاتم الرازي

rows.speaker: ابن عدي
rows.claim: Ibn Adi said al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman was unknown.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عدي: لا يعرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says the report muddles material from different reports; the narrator may have done so deliberately or someone may have inserted it.
rows.anchor: وقد خلط في هذا الحديث، ودخل عليه شيء في شيء، وحديث في حديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the secret and what is still more hidden, so the revelation comes from the Creator who knows all hidden things.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {وإن تجهر بالقول فإنه يعلم السر وأخفى} أي: أنزل هذا القرآن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the secret is what a person conceals inwardly, while what is more hidden is what he will do before he knows it; God's knowledge of past and future is one, and creation is like one person to Him.
rows.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: {يعلم السر وأخفى}

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak defines the secret as one's inner self-talk and what is more hidden as thoughts not yet entertained.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: {يعلم السر وأخفى} قال: السر

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says people know what they think today but not tomorrow, whereas God knows both today's and tomorrow's thoughts.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: أنت تعلم ما تسر اليوم، ولا تعلم ما تسر غدا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets what is more hidden as whispering.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: {وأخفى} يعني: الوسوسة

rows.speaker: مجاهد وسعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr also explain it as what a person will do without having yet thought of it.
rows.anchor: وقال أيضا هو وسعيد بن جبير: {وأخفى} أي: ما هو عامله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The staff transformation is a manifest miracle and break with ordinary nature, proving that only God can do it and that it comes through a sent prophet.
rows.anchor: هذا برهان من الله تعالى لموسى، عليه السلام، ومعجزة عظيمة، وخرق للعادة باهر

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some commentators say God asked about the staff to put Moses at ease.
rows.anchor: قال بعض المفسرين: إنما قال له ذلك على سبيل الإيناس له

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Others take the question as confirmation: God points out that it is the familiar staff in Moses' hand before showing what He will do with it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنما قال له ذلك على وجه التقرير، أي: أما هذه التي في يمينك عصاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses leans on the staff while walking.
rows.anchor: أتوكأ عليها} أي: أعتمد عليها في حال المشي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses shakes branches with the staff so leaves fall for his sheep to eat.
rows.anchor: وأهش بها على غنمي} أي: أهز بها الشجرة ليسقط ورقها

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik defines hashsh as placing the hooked staff in a branch and shaking leaves and fruit down without breaking the branch, unlike striking it.
rows.anchor: عبد الرحمن بن القاسم: عن الإمام مالك: والهش: أن يضع الرجل المحجن

rows.speaker: ميمون بن مهران
rows.claim: Maymun ibn Mihran gives the same explanation of gently shaking a branch to drop its leaves and fruit.
rows.anchor: ولا يكسر العود، فهذا الهش، ولا يخبط. وكذا قال ميمون بن مهران أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Musa's staff served other interests, benefits, and needs besides those he has just named.
rows.anchor: {ولي فيها مآرب أخرى} أي: مصالح ومنافع وحاجات أخر غير ذلك

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some commentators list extraordinary supposed uses: lighting at night, guarding the flock while Moses slept, and growing into a shade tree.
rows.anchor: فقيل: كانت تضيء له بالليل، وتحرس له الغنم إذا نام، ويغرسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir rejects those extraordinary details as apparent Israeli reports: if the staff had such powers, Moses would not have fled when it became a serpent.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنها لم تكن كذلك، ولو كانت كذلك لما استنكر موسى صيرورتها ثعبانا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One reported claim says the staff had belonged to Adam; Ibn Kathir groups such stories with Israeli reports.
rows.anchor: وكذا قول بعضهم: إنها كانت لآدم، عليه السلام

rows.speaker: الآخر
rows.claim: Another reported claim identifies the staff as the beast that will emerge before the Day of Resurrection; Ibn Kathir treats such claims as Israeli reports.
rows.anchor: وقول الآخر: إنها هي الدابة التي تخرج قبل يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas gives the staff the name Masha.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أنه قال: كان اسمها ماشا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tells Moses to throw down the staff in his hand; it immediately becomes a huge, long serpent moving rapidly, as quick as a small jann despite its size.
rows.anchor: ألقها يا موسى} أي: هذه العصا التي في يدك يا موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The serpent's movement is described as walking and thrashing about.
rows.anchor: تسعى} أي: تمشي وتضطرب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the staff had never been a serpent; it swallowed a rock and ate a tree, frightening Moses into flight until God called him three times, after which he took it.
rows.anchor: عن [ابن عباس] (6) {فألقاها فإذا هي حية تسعى} ولم تكن قبل ذلك حية

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih describes an enormous serpent with fiery eyes, teeth, and a mane-like staff hook; Moses fled, returned in fear, and was reassured as he grasped it and it became his staff again.
rows.anchor: وقال وهب بن منبه في قوله: {فألقاها فإذا هي حية تسعى} قال: فألقاها على وجه الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God promises to restore the serpent to the staff's familiar original state.
rows.anchor: ولهذا قال تعالى: {سنعيدها سيرتها الأولى} أي: إلى حالها

rows.speaker: الله
rows.claim: A divine address says the best adornment is worldly renunciation, the pious wear tranquility and humility, and God's true friends should be treated humbly; whoever harms them challenges God, who swiftly aids and avenges them.
rows.anchor: واعلم أنه لا يتزين لي العباد بزينة هي أبلغ مما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks God to expand his heart and ease his task because he has been charged with an immense mission against the most powerful and defiant ruler of his time.
rows.anchor: هذا سؤال من موسى، عليه السلام، لربه عز وجل، أن يشرح له صدره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh claimed not to know God and allowed his subjects no other god; Moses had been raised in Pharaoh's house, then killed one of Pharaoh's people and fled before being sent back to warn them.
rows.anchor: بلغ من أمره أن ادعى أنه لا يعرف الله، ولا يعلم لرعاياه إلها غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses recognizes that he cannot carry out this task unless God is his help, support, and protector.
rows.anchor: إن لم تكن أنت عوني ونصيري، وعضدي وظهيري، وإلا فلا طاقة لي بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After setting a time and place to meet Moses, Pharaoh went to gather magicians from across his cities; magic was widespread and prized, as also stated at 10:79.
rows.anchor: أي: شرع في جمع السحرة من مدائن مملكته، كل من ينسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the appointed festival, Pharaoh sat on his throne amid officials and crowds; Moses arrived with Aaron, and the magicians stood in ranks as Pharaoh urged them on and promised reward and favored status if they won.
rows.anchor: اجتمع الناس لميقات يوم معلوم وهو يوم الزينة، وجلس فرعون على سرير مملكته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses warns the magicians not to deceive people into thinking their illusions create real things, thereby falsely attributing creation to God.
rows.anchor: أي: لا تخيلوا للناس بأعمالكم إيجاد أشياء لا حقائق لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment threatened by Moses is annihilation without remainder.
rows.anchor: أي: يهلككم بعقوبة هلاكا لا بقية له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses adds that anyone who fabricates a lie against God has failed.
rows.anchor: وقد خاب من افترى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation says the magicians argued among themselves: some recognized that Moses spoke as a prophet, while others said he was a magician.
rows.anchor: قيل: معناه: أنهم تشاجروا فيما بينهم فقائل يقول: ليس هذا بكلام ساحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The magicians should gather together in one rank and cast everything at once to dazzle the eyes and overwhelm Moses and Aaron.
rows.anchor: أي اجتمعوا كلكم (1) صفا واحدا، وألقوا ما في أيديكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The magicians imagine that whoever prevails will prosper: they expect Pharaoh's lavish reward, while Moses would gain great authority if he won.
rows.anchor: أي: منا ومنه، أما نحن فقد وعدنا هذا الملك العطاء الجزيل

words: إِنَّآ ءَامَنَّا بِرَبِّنَا لِيَغْفِرَ لَنَا خَطَٰيَٰنَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The magicians ask forgiveness for their sins, especially performing magic under Pharaoh's coercion to counter God's sign and His prophet's miracle.
rows.anchor: أي: ما كان منا من الآثام، خصوصا ما أكرهتنا عليه من السحر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Pharaoh took forty Israelite youths and ordered them trained in magic at al-Farama; they became among the magicians who believed in Moses.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {وما أكرهتنا عليه من السحر} قال: أخذ فرعون أربعين غلاما

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam gives the same account about the Israelite youths trained by Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: وكذا قال عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq's interpretation is that God is better for the magicians than Pharaoh, and God's reward lasts longer than Pharaoh's promise.
rows.anchor: وهو رواية عن ابن إسحاق، رحمه الله.

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi explains that God is better if obeyed and more enduring in punishment if disobeyed.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب القرظي: {والله خير} أي: لنا منك إن أطيع

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says a similar explanation is also narrated from Ibn Ishaq.
rows.anchor: وروي نحوه عن ابن إسحاق أيضا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره من السلف
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and other early authorities said the magicians began the day as magicians and ended it as martyrs, supporting the report that Pharaoh carried out his threat.
rows.anchor: ولهذا قال ابن عباس وغيره من السلف: أصبحوا سحرة، وأمسوا شهداء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir considers it apparent that Pharaoh resolved to execute the magicians and did so.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن فرعون -لعنه الله-صمم على ذلك وفعله بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir takes this as the magicians' continued warning to Pharaoh about God's everlasting punishment and their encouragement toward eternal reward.
rows.anchor: الظاهر من السياق أن هذا من تمام ما وعظ به السحرة لفرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A criminal who meets God on Judgment Day enters Hell, where he neither dies nor lives.
rows.anchor: أي: يلقى الله يوم القيامة وهو مجرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir links this description to verses saying Hell's punishment is not ended by death or lightened, and its inhabitants plead to die but are told they will remain.
rows.anchor: كقوله: {لا يقضى عليهم فيموتوا ولا يخفف عنهم من عذابها

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: The Prophet says those destined to remain in Hell neither die nor live; sinful people are burned to charcoal, then intercessors bring them in groups to Paradise's rivers, where they sprout like flood-carried seeds. Ahmad transmits it and Muslim includes it in his Sahih.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "أما أهل النار الذين هم أهلها

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: A second report says the Prophet cited this verse in a sermon: those destined for Hell never die, while others are touched by the fire, then intercessors bring them to the river of Life, where they grow like cucumbers in a flood.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خطب فأتى على هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gardens of Eden means a permanent abode and is in apposition to the lofty degrees promised in the preceding verse.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {جنات عدن تجري} أي: إقامة وهو بدل من الدرجات العلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of these gardens remain there forever.
rows.anchor: خالدين فيها} (2) أي: ماكثين أبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the reward of one who purifies himself from stain, evil, and shirk, worships God alone, and believes the messengers' reports and commands.
rows.anchor: وذلك جزاء من تزكى} أي: طهر نفسه من الدنس والخبث والشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because resurrection and recompense are certain, God sent the Qur'an as warning and good news in clear, eloquent Arabic without ambiguity or faltering.
rows.anchor: يقول: ولما كان يوم المعاد والجزاء بالخير والشر واقعا لا محالة، أنزلنا القرآن بشيرا ونذيرا، بلسان عربي مبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warnings may lead people to avoid sins, forbidden acts, and indecencies, or to remember through obedience and devotional acts.
rows.anchor: أي: يتركون المآثم والمحارم والفواحش، {أو يحدث لهم ذكرا} وهو إيجاد الطاعة وفعل القربات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is exalted and holy as the true King; He, His promise and threat, His messengers, Paradise, Hell, and everything from Him are true.
rows.anchor: أي: تنزه وتقدس (3) الملك الحق، الذي هو حق، ووعده حق، ووعيده حق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's justice means He does not punish anyone before warning them and sending messengers, leaving no excuse or doubt.
rows.anchor: وعدله تعالى ألا يعذب أحدا قبل الإنذار وبعثة الرسل والإعذار إلى خلقه

words: وَلَا تَعْجَلْ بِٱلْقُرْءَانِ مِن قَبْلِ أَن يُقْضَىٰٓ إِلَيْكَ وَحْيُهُۥ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir connects this command to 75:16-19, where God tells the Prophet not to move his tongue hastily during revelation and promises its collection and explanation.
rows.anchor: كقوله تعالى في سورة "لا أقسم بيوم القيامة" {لا تحرك به لسانك لتعجل به * إن علينا جمعه

words: وَلَا تَعْجَلْ بِٱلْقُرْءَانِ مِن قَبْلِ أَن يُقْضَىٰٓ إِلَيْكَ وَحْيُهُۥ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: An authentic report from Ibn Abbas says revelation was difficult for the Prophet, who repeated Gabriel's words from concern to memorize them; God instructed him to listen until the angel finished, then recite.
rows.anchor: وثبت في الصحيح عن ابن عباس؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يعالج من الوحي شدة

words: وَلَا تَعْجَلْ بِٱلْقُرْءَانِ مِن قَبْلِ أَن يُقْضَىٰٓ إِلَيْكَ وَحْيُهُۥ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is to listen until the angel completes the revelation, then recite; God will gather it in the Prophet's breast so he does not forget it, and explain it.
rows.anchor: أي: بل أنصت، فإذا فرغ الملك من قراءته عليك فاقرأه بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is instructed to ask God to increase him in knowledge.
rows.anchor: أي: زدني منك علما

rows.speaker: ابن عيينة
rows.claim: Ibn Uyayna says the Prophet's knowledge continued increasing until God took his life.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عيينة، رحمه الله: ولم يزل صلى الله عليه وسلم في زيادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir cites a report that revelation continued coming to the Messenger until it was at its greatest volume on the day he died.
rows.anchor: إن الله تابع الوحي على رسوله، حتى كان الوحي أكثر ما كان يوم توفي رسول الله

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet prayed: O God, benefit me by what You taught me, teach me what benefits me, increase my knowledge, and praise belongs to God in every state; Ibn Majah transmits it.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن ماجه: حدثنا أبو بكر بن أبي شيبة، حدثنا عبد الله بن نمير، عن موسى بن عبيدة، عن محمد بن ثابت، عن أبي هريرة، رضي الله عنه، قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "اللهم انفعني بما علمتني

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhi transmits Abu Hurayra's prayer report and calls it unusual by this route; al-Bazzar also transmits it and adds a plea for refuge from the condition of the people of Hell.
rows.anchor: وأخرجه الترمذي، عن أبي كريب، عن عبد الله بن نمير، به. وقال: غريب من هذا الوجه.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the human being was named insan because he was charged with a covenant and then forgot it; Ibn Kathir notes another transmission from Ibn Abbas through Ali ibn Abi Talha.
rows.anchor: قال ابن أبي حاتم: حدثنا أحمد بن سنان، حدثنا أسباط بن محمد، حدثنا الأعمش، عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس قال: إنما سمي الإنسان لأنه عهد إليه فنسي.

rows.speaker: مجاهد والحسن
rows.claim: Mujahid and al-Hasan understand nasiya here to mean that Adam abandoned or neglected the command.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد والحسن: ترك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to the angels recalls God's honoring Adam and preferring him above many creatures.
rows.anchor: يذكر تعالى تشريف آدم وتكريمه، وما فضله به على كثير ممن خلق تفضيلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says Adam's story was discussed in al-Baqara, al-Araf, al-Hijr, and al-Kahf, and will be revisited at the end of Sad.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم الكلام على هذه القصة في سورة "البقرة" وفي "الأعراف" وفي "الحجر" و"الكهف" (1) وسيأتي في آخر سورة "ص"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis refused to prostrate and acted arrogantly.
rows.anchor: أي: امتنع واستكبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The enemy addressed is Iblis, and Adam's wife is Hawwa.
rows.anchor: يعني: حواء، عليهما السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God warns Adam not to let Iblis strive to expel them from Paradise, where Adam enjoys ease, lest he toil and suffer seeking his livelihood.
rows.anchor: أي: إياك أن يسعى (5) في إخراجك منها، فتتعب وتعنى وتشقى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hunger and nakedness are paired because hunger is inward humiliation and nakedness is outward humiliation.
rows.anchor: إنما قرن بين الجوع والعري؛ لأن الجوع ذل الباطن، والعري ذل الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thirst and exposure to the sun are paired: thirst is heat within, while dahwa is heat on the outside.
rows.anchor: وهذان أيضا متقابلان، فالظمأ: حر الباطن، وهو العطش. والضحى: حر الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir recalls the earlier account that Satan deluded Adam and his wife and swore he was their sincere adviser.
rows.anchor: قد تقدم أنه (7) {دلاهما بغرور} [الأعراف: 22] ؛ {وقاسمهما إني لكما لمن الناصحين}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God permitted Adam and his wife every fruit except one specified tree; Satan persisted until they ate from it, calling it the tree of eternity because its eater would remain forever.
rows.anchor: أوحى إلى آدم وزوجته أن يأكلا من كل الثمار، ولا يقربا هذه الشجرة المعينة في الجنة

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet says Paradise has a tree whose shade a rider could travel through for a hundred years without crossing it; it is called the tree of eternity. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi and Ahmad transmit it.
rows.anchor: قال أبو داود الطيالسي: حدثنا شعبة عن أبي الضحاك (1) سمعت أبا هريرة يحدث، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "إن في الجنة شجرة

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: A report attributed to Ubayy ibn Ka'b says Adam was tall and hairy; after tasting the tree his clothes fell, he ran in shame, and a tree caught his hair. He asked God if repentance would return him to Paradise, and God said yes.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، عن الحسن، عن أبي بن كعب قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إن الله خلق آدم رجلا طوالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says the report is disconnected between al-Hasan and Ubayy, and its attribution to the Prophet is also questionable.
